description: Arabic (Modern Standard Arabic) glossary of the game's own text (docs/modding/translation-handbook.md). terms: English term of glossary_en.json -> the Arabic form used in every file. keep_latin: Latin words the validator accepts in the Arabic text. style: the rules of voice and form.

style.script: Stored in logical order, unshaped: plain letters of the Arabic block, no presentation forms, no tatweel, no directional control characters, no harakat (tanwin and shadda are not written: شكرا, جدا). Western digits. Punctuation ؟ ، ؛ and the ASCII . ! : ...
style.address: Arabic has no formal/informal pronoun; the register carries the distance. Harry and Cybil, Harry and Lisa: plain, direct. Harry and Kaufmann: curt and distant, Kaufmann introduces himself as الدكتور. Dahlia to everyone: elevated classical diction (إني, هاك, أجل, علمت أنك آت). Alessa to Dahlia: ماما; Cheryl to Harry: بابا.
style.gender: Verbs, adjectives and imperatives carry the gender of the speaker and of the person spoken to: every line needs both (see the list of scenes in translation-handbook.md). The player is addressed in the masculine singular (هل تأخذه؟). The ending with the aliens is in the plural; the writings on the walls of Alessa's room are in the feminine.
style.quotes: « » for the [ ] of the English (the layout engine mirrors them in a right-to-left line); the dash is the character — (U+2014), which the English writes as '='.
style.item_in_sentence: an item name inside a sentence is the inventory name unchanged, indefinite: 'يوجد هنا <name>. هل تأخذه؟ / هل تأخذها؟' (the pronoun follows the gender of the item), 'استخدمت <name>.', 'حصلت على <name>.'
style.names: Names of people and places are transliterated (هاري ميسون); only PTV stays in Latin letters.

terms.There is a X. Take it?: يوجد هنا <X>. هل تأخذه؟ / هل تأخذها؟
